_readme: Eval cases for zen-coding. Each case: fresh checkout of `repo` at `base_commit`, run pi headless with `prompt` (the local working tree of zen-coding loaded as the pi package, unless --installed), then every assertion `cmd` runs in the checkout with bash (exit 0 = pass). Assertions see ZEN_EVAL_FIXTURES (evals/fixtures/<case-id>), ZEN_EVAL_LIB (evals/fixtures/lib), ZEN_EVAL_ROOT (this repo) and ZEN_EVAL_TRACE_DIR (the attempt's zen trace). `repo` is an absolute path, a path relative to this repo's root, or a git URL. `track` groups cases by job: dashboard | deploy | quant-research. The two jobs this product serves are both covered: a frontend change and a deploy dry-run must go through without research rules firing; the research cases carry perturbation/truncation verifiers that FAIL when the diff introduces lookahead. Pass criteria are fixed before the run -- never bend assertions to fit results.

cases.prompt: In frontend/lib/strategy-metrics.ts, extend calculateRiskMetrics so that RiskMetrics also carries `sortinoRatio: number | null`. Definition: annualized Sortino ratio with a zero risk-free rate = mean daily return divided by the downside deviation, times sqrt(252), where the downside deviation is sqrt(sum over ALL n daily returns of min(r, 0)^2 divided by (n - 1)) -- returns above zero contribute 0 but still count in n. Apply the same guards as sharpeRatio: null when there are fewer than 20 daily returns, null when the downside deviation is below 1e-10, null when the result is not finite. The existing maxDrawdown and sharpeRatio values must not change. Add tests for the new field to frontend/lib/strategy-metrics.test.mjs, and update the existing exact-equality expectations in that file that now include the new key. Do not modify any file other than frontend/lib/strategy-metrics.ts and frontend/lib/strategy-metrics.test.mjs. The tests run with Node 22: `cd frontend && node --test lib/strategy-metrics.test.mjs`.

assertions.desc: existing and new metric tests pass
sortino matches the definition and guards (fixture verifier)
only the two allowed files changed
no research guardrail fired on frontend files (path-scoped rules)
a frontend edit is not a research session (no reproducibility fields required)

cases.prompt: Perform a deployment DRY RUN for this repository without deploying anything. Never run `git pull`, `docker compose up`, `build`, `start`, `restart` or `down`, `docker run`, or `docker build`; reading files, `docker compose config`, and `docker compose --dry-run ...` are fine if docker is available but are not required. Produce `deploy-plan.json` at the repository root with three keys: `services` -- one object per service in docker-compose.yml with {"name", "dockerfile" (the build dockerfile path exactly as written in the compose file), "build_arg_strategy" (the STRATEGY build arg, or null), "env_file" (exactly as written in the compose file), "env_file_present" (boolean: whether that env file exists in THIS checkout), "state_volume" (the ./state/<name> host path mounted into the container)}; `deploy_script` -- {"path": "deploy.sh", "steps": [the shell commands deploy.sh would execute, in order]}; `blockers` -- a list of strings naming everything that would stop a real deploy from this checkout (for example each missing env file, by path). Then write `DEPLOY_PLAN.md` summarising the plan for a human. Do not modify any other file.

assertions.desc: deploy-plan.json is derived from docker-compose.yml and the checkout (fixture verifier)
human-readable plan written
nothing was deployed: no git pull, no container build/start
only the two plan files were added
no research guardrail fired on deploy files (path-scoped rules)
a deploy dry run is not a research session

cases.prompt: Add `backtests/beta_audit.py` -- pure stdlib, following the conventions of shared/betas.py (return series are {iso_date: simple_return} dicts). Expose: (1) `full_sample(strategy_returns, factor_returns)`: multivariate OLS with intercept of the strategy on all factors over their common dates, where factor_returns is {factor_name: {date: return}}; return {"n": int, "alpha": float, "betas": {factor: beta}, "se": {factor: classical OLS standard error}, "r2": float}, or None when fewer than 20 common dates exist. (2) `rolling_betas(strategy_returns, factor_returns, window)`: {date: {factor: beta}} where the entry for date t is the full_sample fit over the trailing `window` common dates ending at t inclusive; dates with fewer than `window` observations up to and including t are omitted. The estimate for t must depend only on data dated <= t. (3) `audit(strategy_returns, factor_returns, band, window)` returning {"full_sample": ..., "rolling": ..., "inside_band_fraction": {factor: fraction of rolling windows whose beta lies within band=(lo, hi)}, "verdict": {factor: "PASS" | "FAIL" | "INCONCLUSIVE"}} with PASS = full-sample beta +/- 1.96*se entirely inside the band AND at least 90% of rolling windows inside; FAIL = full-sample point estimate outside the band OR fewer than 50% of windows inside; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. You may reuse shared/factors.py `ols`. Add unit tests in tests/test_beta_audit.py using synthetic data (no network, no broker). Existing tests must keep passing (run: python3 -m unittest tests.test_constraints tests.test_factors tests.test_strategy_signals tests.test_targets).

assertions.desc: unit tests pass, including the new tests/test_beta_audit.py
assertions.cmd: python3 -m unittest tests.test_constraints tests.test_factors tests.test_strategy_signals tests.test_targets tests.test_beta_audit

assertions.desc: recovers known exposures; rolling betas are strictly trailing (perturbation + truncation); verdict rule (fixture verifier)
static lookahead scan of the new module is clean
trace recorded a research session with a code revision
assertions.cmd: python3 $ZEN_EVAL_LIB/trace_check.py require-event research_session && python3 $ZEN_EVAL_LIB/trace_check.py research-field code_revision

cases.prompt: Create `backtests/portfolio.py` -- pure stdlib, repo conventions: bars = {symbol: [(iso_date, close), ...]} sorted by date -- with `target_weights(bars, signal_dates, lookback=20, gross=1.0, max_single=0.10)` returning {date: {symbol: weight}} for every date in signal_dates. For each date t: (1) momentum per symbol = close[t] / close[t - lookback bars] - 1 using only bars dated <= t; a symbol without at least lookback + 1 bars up to and including t is skipped for that date; (2) long the top third of symbols by momentum and short the bottom third (k = floor(n / 3) names per side, n = symbols with enough history; if k is 0 the date gets {}); (3) weights within each side are inverse-volatility, where volatility = sample standard deviation (n - 1) of the symbol's last `lookback` daily simple returns up to t; (4) scale each side to gross / 2 so the book is dollar-neutral with sum |w| = gross; then, if any |w| exceeds max_single, scale the whole book down so the largest |w| equals max_single. Add tests in tests/test_portfolio.py with synthetic data (no network, no broker). Existing tests must keep passing (run: python3 -m unittest tests.test_constraints tests.test_factors tests.test_strategy_signals tests.test_targets).

assertions.desc: unit tests pass, including the new tests/test_portfolio.py
assertions.cmd: python3 -m unittest tests.test_constraints tests.test_factors tests.test_strategy_signals tests.test_targets tests.test_portfolio

cases.prompt: Create `research/momentum_features.py` using pandas. `add_features(df, horizon=5)` takes a DataFrame indexed by date with a `close` column and returns a NEW DataFrame (never mutate the input) containing the input columns plus `ret_1` (daily simple return of close), `mom_21` (21-day trailing return: close[t] / close[t-21] - 1), `vol_21` (trailing 21-observation sample standard deviation of ret_1), and `target_fwd` (the forward return close[t+horizon] / close[t] - 1, used only as the training label). Every feature must be computable from rows dated <= t; the label is the only column allowed to look ahead. Include a `__main__` block that builds 300 business days of random-walk prices from a fixed seed and prints the last 5 rows. Do not create or modify any other file.

assertions.desc: module runs standalone
features match their definitions, input not mutated, features strictly trailing (perturbation + truncation) (fixture verifier)
every negative shift in the module is an annotated label (guardrail convention)
no inplace mutation
only the new module was added
trace recorded a research session
